name: GPT-IMG
tagline: A web app for generating and editing images with OpenAI's image models from a browser prompt box.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a front end for a model somebody else trained. The hard part, the image model, is an API call, and the app around it is a prompt box, an aspect ratio picker, a credits counter, and a gallery. An agent can produce a local version in one sitting that writes files to your own disk and never expires your credits. The honest catch is that you are not escaping the dependency, you are just moving it: you pay OpenAI per image instead of paying a reseller per month, which usually works out cheaper unless you generate almost nothing. What you give up is the polish, the preset library, and someone else absorbing the rate limits.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you type a prompt, pick a size, call the OpenAI image API with your own key, and get the result saved to disk with its prompt in a searchable gallery.
requirements: An OpenAI API key with image generation access and billing enabled
Node 20+ and somewhere to run it, local machine is fine
Disk space, generated PNGs add up fast
whatYouLose: Per-image billing surprises are now yours to watch, no monthly cap protecting you from a loop that fires 400 requests
Curated style presets and prompt templates that actually work, you start from a blank box
Any mobile experience beyond a browser pointed at your laptop
Content moderation handling and graceful failure messages when a prompt gets refused
Model swaps, when a better endpoint ships someone has to go update your code
moatNotes: The model moat belongs to OpenAI, not to the wrapper. Resellers compete on UI, presets, and the convenience of not holding an API key.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because an API key is a small but real wall. Plenty of people want to type a sentence and get a picture without creating a developer account, loading credits, or thinking about tokens at all, and a flat monthly number is easier to reason about than metered usage. Preset galleries also do more work than people admit: half the value of these sites is a prompt someone else already tuned. If you generate a handful of images a month and never want to see a billing dashboard, paying a few dollars for the smoothed-over version is a defensible trade.
notes: A prompt box, a fetch call, and a folder of PNGs, sold monthly.
prompt:
Build a local-only AI image studio. No accounts, no cloud database, no telemetry, no analytics.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router and TypeScript
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- better-sqlite3 for a local gallery index at ./data/gallery.db
- Generated images written as files to ./data/images, served through a route handler
- OPENAI_API_KEY read from .env.local, never hardcoded, never sent anywhere except api.openai.com

Features that are in scope:
1. A single page with a prompt textarea, a size selector (1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536), a quality selector, and a count selector from 1 to 4.
2. Generate calls the OpenAI images API server side only. The key must never reach the browser.
3. Each result is saved to disk as a PNG with a ULID filename, and a row is inserted with prompt, size, quality, model, cost estimate, and created timestamp.
4. A gallery grid below the form showing newest first, with infinite scroll or a simple paginated load more.
5. Click an image to open a detail view with the full prompt, a copy prompt button, a reuse prompt button that refills the form, and a delete button that removes both the row and the file.
6. Full text search across stored prompts using SQLite FTS5.
7. An edit mode: upload or pick an existing image plus an optional mask and a prompt, call the image edit endpoint, save the result linked to its parent.
8. A running spend estimate for the current month, computed from stored rows using a price table in a single config file that is easy to update.

Out of scope, do not build: user auth, multi-tenancy, payment handling, local model inference, a prompt preset marketplace, social sharing.

Handle API refusals and rate limits by surfacing the actual error text in the UI instead of a generic toast. Include a README with setup steps, a .env.example, and a note that ./data should be gitignored.
